name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with an 18-point partisan lean
Incumbent Jonathan Jackson running for reelection
Huge fundraising gap: Jackson raised $418K vs. Maxwell's $63K
Prediction markets price Jackson at 96% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Jackson: a heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage over a little-known, underfunded challenger. Markets agree, pricing his win odds near 96%, so there is no evidence to move the forecast from the fundamentals-based expectation of a roughly 24-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise wave-style national environment or an unexpectedly well-funded late challenger effort could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jonathan Jackson, the Democratic incumbent in this heavily Democratic Chicago-area district, is running for reelection against Republican Christian Maxwell. The seat leans Democratic by 18 points, and Jackson holds a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $418,000 to Maxwell's $63,000. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Jackson about a 96% chance of winning.

With no polling and no outside spending reported, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. All of these point the same way: a comfortable Democratic win with an expected margin in the low-to-mid 20s and only a small chance of an upset.
